The visual-evidence skill requires comparing the best finite result with an informative failure and cross-checking the images against metrics/diagnostics. I’m now loading the assigned guidance, sampled result inventory, inherited optimizer notes, and candidate baseline before making any edits.

All four current sampled solvers converge on the same successful behavior: target capture at 88.13 release units, 0.747 L final distance, and identical force/flow metrics. The useful contrast is therefore in inherited logs: three earlier phase/headroom-only variants exited the upper domain after ~71–73 units. I’m inspecting those failure sheets alongside the common prewarm and successful release sheet, then I’ll isolate one evidence-supported next change.

The evidence isolates one clean next bracket. The successful `0.18` cross-track term is now reproduced four times and is the only mechanism that changes the upper-exit topology, but the keyframe sheet still shows a broad midcourse return toward the upper wake before capture. I’ll test only a small gain increase to `0.20`, keeping the proven propulsion, phase allocation, damping, fades, and limits unchanged. The hypothesis is faster/more direct capture; loss of capture or higher load without lower distance integral will falsify it.

The candidate, provenance notes, and durable guidance are now updated. The reusable lesson records the reproduced success as deterministic confirmation (not four robustness trials), supersedes the phase-only anchor, and preserves the exact `0.18` controller as the rollback boundary.
